_readme: Every reward, price and shop rule lives here. Edit numbers, save, reload the game. The game reads 'rewards', 'events' and 'shop'. All shop items below are PLACEHOLDER test data - names, prices and effects are just there so the shop has something to show (effects are not applied yet). See docs/ECONOMY.md for what every field means, and run 'py tools/economy_report.py' for a quick balance table.

rewards._note: The base coins for hitting each window come from the projectile in use - see 'projectiles' below (rewards.W20 / rewards.W21). The streak is only a counter now: it adds no coins.

events._rarityNote: EVENT RARITIES: an event has the rarity of its SUMMON BUFF (the shop item whose triggerEvent effect names the event: Tomato Juice -> face: EPIC, Disco Ticket -> disco: LEGENDARY); an event with no such buff can name its rarity in its own block ("rarity"). NATURAL SPAWNING: after every throw the game rolls ONE independent chance for each RARITY that has events (not for each event); if several rarities hit on the same throw the BETTER (rarer) one wins; the winning rarity picks one of its events at random - so adding an event never makes its rarity more frequent. The chance of a rarity is worked out so that, on average, it takes as many throws to get one of its events as it takes to see an item of that rarity in the shop: meanShopHours = 1 / (share of the rarity in the shop's rarity roll x slots x 3600 / availabilitySeconds), chance per throw = 1 / (meanShopHours x throwsPerHour). throwsPerHour is the snowball's real refill rate, 3600 / projectiles.snowball.regen.everySeconds = 120 an hour (so it follows the regen; set events.throwsPerHour to override it). With today's shop odds (common 60, rare 30, epic 9, legendary 1 of 100): common about 1 in 17 throws, rare 1 in 33, epic 1 in 111 (the banana face or the guitar, a coin toss between them), legendary 1 in 1000 (the disco). A rarity that has no item in the shop cannot spawn. To set a rarity's chance by hand add events.rarityChances { legendary: 0.0008 }.
events._discoNote: DISCO event (see main.js startDiscoEvent): legendary like its summon buff (see _rarityNote for how often it spawns by itself). While disco.mp3 plays (about 2:44) W20 shows discoface1-6 (a new one every beatMs = 500 ms, 120 bpm); a hit on the singer's FACE pays faceMultiplier x the coins of that throw (it is fixed, and the face stays, so every hit of the song counts: it is far below the banana face's x2.5 because it can pay many times); a plain W20 hit pays as usual. Afterwards applause.mp3 plays while roses fall, then everything is normal.
events._guitarNote: GUITAR event (the same idea as the disco, see main.js SONG_EVENTS): EPIC (it has no summon buff, so its own rarity below names it; it shares the epic events' natural chance with the banana face - see _rarityNote). While guitar.mp3 plays W20 cycles guitar1 -> guitar2 -> guitar3 (a new one every beatMs); a hit on the guitarist's FACE pays faceMultiplier x the coins of that throw (fixed, the face stays, so every hit of the song counts); a plain W20 hit pays as usual. Afterwards applause.mp3 plays while roses fall, then everything is normal.

_skinsNote: SKINS (the SKINS button, between PROJECTILES and OPTIONS): characters, sceneries and weather (see _weatherNote) are equipped, and each may carry `effects` [{type, value}] that are on for as long as it is equipped (coinMultiplier and offsetCenter, read like a buff's by buffs.js modifiers() - none uses them today; shopSpeed: the shop's timers - the item's availability timer and the sold-out timer - run value x as fast, on a clock that goes on while the app is closed: Economy.shopNow(), Frosty Night 1.2 = a 30 minute timer takes 25), never consumed, never unequipped (only by equipping another one), and listed by rarity, the rarest first. characters: the thrower; `character` names its entry in CHARACTERS (main.js: the empty-handed pictures and hand numbers), `image` is the face on its card, `detail` will describe the bonus it gives (empty for the default one). sceneries: the picture behind the game; `background` is the wall texture - it must be EXACTLY the size of assets/building/background.png (704x1000) with the windows in the same places, so a scenery is only a visual change; `image` is its card picture. rarity: one of the rarities below (default = free, always owned); others must be unlocked (Economy.unlock).

_weatherNote: WEATHER (the third skins category, the WEATHER button in the SKINS list): particles that fall from the sky over the whole game picture - the same way the roses fall in the disco / guitar applause (they start at the top of the world, fall straight down and leave below the bottom of the default view) - for as long as the weather is equipped. It is equipped, never consumed, never unequipped (only by equipping another one - there is always a weather), and listed by rarity like the other skins. weathers: id, name, description, image (the card picture), particle (the falling picture, any size: it is drawn particleSize px wide, each one a little bigger or smaller), particleSize, angle (degrees from straight down the particles fall at: 0 = straight down, positive = towards the right, so 65 is a fast wind-blown fall from the left to the right; the spawn also comes in over the left edge), sway (px the particle swings from side to side while it falls; 0 = none), drift (the most px a second a particle drifts sideways, each rolls its own between -drift and +drift; 0 or missing = none: straight down), rarity (default = free, always owned; others must be unlocked, Economy.unlock('weather', id)), detail (the bottom line of the card - NOT the density or the speed: the card does not tell them). effects (optional, like a buff's: what equipping it does - none of the weathers has one today: the Blizzard is purely visual; an offsetCenter effect, the offset slider's hit zone centered elsewhere than the middle of the bar, is still supported). density and fallSpeed are NAMES of the two scales below. weatherDensities: how many particles are in the game picture (432 x 243) at any moment; the spawn rate follows from it and the fall speed (density x average speed / 243 a second), so a slow weather does not look thinner than a fast one. The roses of the applause are 30 at once (spawned at 30 a second, falling 200-300 px/s) - that is 'heavy' density and 'moderate' fall speed. weatherSpeeds: px a second, each particle rolls its own between from and to (very_slow 25-40, slow 50-75, moderate 200-300 like the roses, fast 400-550, very_fast 700-900; for a slanted weather this is the speed ALONG its path).
_aimNote: Speed of the two aim markers (offset and strength - always the same, fixed speed). markerHz = full back-and-forth sweeps per second (1.275 = one sweep in ~0.8s; it was 0.85 = ~1.2s). Nothing changes it: not the streak, not the projectile; only the Triangles buffs slow the OFFSET marker (effect offsetSpeed). (The width of the offset slider's hit zone comes from the projectile's weight tier, see weightTiers / offsetZone.)
_buffCapsNote: Buffs of the same kind STACK. saveProjectile: several save chances are INDEPENDENT ROLLS (10% and 20% together = 1 - 0.9 x 0.8 = 28%), the total never goes above this share (0.9) - the only cap. Coin multipliers multiply each other (1.1 x 1.2 = 1.32) and offsetSpeed slow-downs multiply (0.9 x 0.8 = 0.72), both WITHOUT a limit.
_rarityNote: Every projectile (in "projectiles") and every buff (in the shop items) has a rarity number, bigger = rarer: the PROJECTILES and BUFFS tabs list the rarest first (equal rarities: projectiles by W20 hit value, buffs in file order). The numbers are PLACEHOLDERS - 1, 2, 3 in the current order - to be decided later.
_weightTiersNote: PROJECTILE WEIGHT is a tier, not a number. from-to: where on the STRENGTH slider a throw of that projectile lands in W20 (shares of the slider, 0 = its start, 1 = its tip) - very light 0-25%, light 25-50%, moderate 37.5-62.5%, heavy 50-75%, very heavy 75-100%; every band is 25% wide. offsetZone: the share of the OFFSET slider (the whole bar) that is a guaranteed W20 hit, centered on the middle of the bar and reaching out to both sides - very light 6.25%, light 12.5%, moderate 25%, heavy 12.5%, very heavy 6.25% (since 2026-09-21 the heavy tiers are the precise ones: a heavy projectile has the light one's zone, a very heavy the very light one's). The bar is scaled so the hit zone fills exactly that share, so a smaller offsetZone = a longer, less precise swing. A buff with the effect type precision multiplies the zone (1.2 = 20% bigger: 25% becomes 30%, never more than 100%). label is the word on the projectile's card. A projectile names its tier in projectiles.<id>.weight.
_raritiesNote: Rarities, from the lowest to the rarest. projectileHitValue: what ONE HIT pays (base coins, before buffs and events) with a projectile of this rarity - the same for both goal windows and for every projectile of the rarity: default (the snowball) 4, common 16, rare 128, epic 960, legendary 4800 (a standard stack is 3-7 pieces at a price per piece 8 / 60 / 450 / 2250 up to 12 / 100 / 750 / 3750, average 10 / 80 / 600 / 3000, so the hit value is always above the highest price; a stack costs 50 / 400 / 3000 / 15000 on average). A projectile can override it with its own hitValue - the HEAVY HITTERS do (Stone 40, Egg 320, Grenade 2400): a smaller stack (1-3 instead of 3-7), a price per piece 2.5x higher and a hit value 2.5x higher, for the same average stack price - higher risk, higher reward. availabilitySeconds: how long an item of that rarity stays on sale in the shop before its slot REROLLS (a new item, amount and price) - 30 min for every rarity (better rarity no longer means longer); the timer is shown on the card and runs on the device clock (also while the app is closed); a rarity without it (default) has no timer. default (light grey, chance 0) is the snowball's: it can never come up in the shop. For the others a shop slot first rolls a rarity by chance (percent - only rarities that have an item to sell take part, and their chances are rescaled to 100), then picks one of that rarity's items at random. color is CSS text colour, or rainbow (animated waves + a pulsing shine). Every projectile (in projectiles) and every shop item names one with rarity; the PROJECTILES and BUFFS tabs list the rarest first and an item with NO rarity always goes at the very end, after default and common.
_projectilesNote: Gameplay settings for every projectile you can equip (the id must match its shop item / its entry in the PROJECTILES list). regen { max, everySeconds }: a refilling stock (the snowball): the player starts with max, every one thrown is given back at one per everySeconds (by the device clock, also while the app is closed), and its card never leaves the list even at 0. infinite: true = never runs out (none right now). Every other projectile is a CONSUMABLE: one is used up the moment the player taps TAP to aim, and it is NOT given back if the aim is abandoned; when the last one is gone the snowball is equipped again. rarity: its tier - it decides the HIT VALUE (see rarities.projectileHitValue). weight: the WEIGHT TIER (see weightTiers): where on the strength slider it hits W20 and how wide the offset slider is. Shown to the player as the tier word. leavesMark: false = no snow mark, it bounces off instead. spins: it rotates in flight.

shop._priceOverrideNote: PLACEHOLDER: while priceOverride is a number, EVERY item costs that many coins in the shop (so we can test buying). Set it to null to use each item's real 'price' below.
shop._restockNote: After buying, that slot shows SOLD OUT for this many seconds (by the device clock, so it also counts while the app is closed), then restocks. 1800 = 30 minutes (60 = 1 minute is handy for testing; 3600 = 1 hour).
shop._buffMaxNote: Optional: the most copies of ONE buff the player can hold; buying one they are already maxed on is refused like too little money (the card shakes, nothing is charged). Not set now = no limit. Add "buffMax": 99 to bring the old cap back.
shop._itemsNote: Empty slots show (TBD) - the shop only has real items now. Optional item field image = a picture path for the card. Consumables are timed BUFFS: bought = active right away for duration.seconds, with a list of effects (guideLines, precision, strengthControl, coinMultiplier - see src/buffs.js). a single item can have priceRange {min, max} instead of price: its price is rolled in that range each time it is put on sale. category is 'consumable' (a timed buff: can be on sale in several slots at once; needs a duration) or 'projectile' (a stack of consumable projectiles: each time it is put on sale the amount (amount.min..max) and the price of ONE (unitPrice.min..max) are rolled at random, the slot's price is amount x unitPrice; the same stack can be on sale in several slots at once, each with its own roll).
